_comment: Pre-warming for the build cache.
The cache fills itself as people use the site: anything built is stored and
served instantly the next time someone asks for the same structure at the
same settings. This file front-runs that for the structures we already know
will be asked for -- a lookup is 0.11 ms against tens of seconds of marching
cubes, so an entry here is the difference between a visitor waiting and a
visitor never learning there was anything to wait for.
This list used to be empty, which meant the script ran and did nothing.
The six example chips on the front page are built at three scales each,
because scale_mm_per_angstrom is part of the cache key and it is the one
control people actually move -- pinning a single scale only helps a visitor
who touches nothing. The rest are the default scale only; add more as the
logs justify them.
Deliberately absent: anything capsid-sized (6VXX and friends). Those are
tens of minutes each and nobody arrives expecting them to be instant.
Mind the size. One large complex is 40-60 MB across its 3MF, GLB and STL
zip, so this list is roughly 1-1.5 GB. Check it against
PDB2PRINT_CACHE_MAX_GB before running.
Every entry has to be rebuilt after CACHE_VERSION changes:
python scripts/pregenerate.py --force
Fields: pdb_id, preset (a name from pdb2print/presets.py), and optional
overrides (PrintParams fields; 'connections' may be given as an object).
